decisions.note: Round-1 spec warned on duplicate save; client rejected the dead-end warning and supplied the reference behavior (open existing bookmark for edit) — spec gate.
Round-1 spec proposed title-only fetch; client supplied the correct scope (description, favicon, preview image, editable description) — spec gate.
Round-1 spec never mentioned that clicking a bookmark opens the url; client surfaced this missing reference item — spec gate.
Round-1 spec described only plain-word search; client requested case-insensitivity, quoted exact-phrase, and AND/NOT tag combination not surfaced by maker — spec gate.
Tag autocomplete/suggestion was absent from round-1 spec; client asked for it explicitly — spec gate.
Round-1 spec only implied a default sort; client asked for sort-by-title/oldest options — spec gate.
Read-later/unread flag and its own view were absent from round-1 spec; client requested it — spec gate.
Round-1 spec's edit story covered title/notes/tags but not the url itself; client asked to also fix the address — spec gate.
Only permanent delete was in round-1 spec; client asked for reversible archive distinct from delete — spec gate.
Round-2 spec only added AND/NOT tag filters; client asked for OR and mixed and/or/not combinations — spec gate.
Bulk/batch actions on selection or whole filtered collection were absent from round-2 spec; client requested them — spec gate.
Saved search/bundle reuse was absent from round-2 spec; client requested saving a search+tag combination — spec gate.
Markdown note rendering (headings/bullets/links) was absent from round-2 spec; client requested it — spec gate.
No export/import/backup capability existed anywhere in spec or plan through round 3; client surfaced the need at the plan gate.
Round-5 backup presentation omitted whether original saved dates survive import; client asked specifically, catching the gap against the reference's 'preserving date added' clause — plan gate.

Shipped US1 MVP (round 7) silently dropped the already-approved save-time title/tag/note entry and the editable-description capability; client caught the runtime regression against approved spec and got it restored in round 8.

satisficing_misses.note: Reference requires Netscape HTML import/export; implementation (rounds 5/10) shipped a JSON file instead, and the client affirmed it purely on 'peace of mind' grounds without noticing the format mismatch — runtime, satisficing miss.

Reference specifies boolean AND/OR/NOT with parenthesised groups typed in the search string, plus a rule that operators must be quoted to be literal; implementation substituted a tag-chip cycle UI and the AND-stacking-with-text-search behavior was only spot-checked (round 9-10) — the quoting/parenthesis nuance was never raised by either side, a satisficing miss.
